title: PowerShell suspicious execution investigation pattern
content: Correlate the PowerShell process with its parent, user, host, command-line representation, script-block or module telemetry, child processes, network destinations, and the first-seen baseline. A suspicious flag alone is a lead: preserve the returned event identifiers and time window, then pivot only on fields actually present in the evidence.

title: PowerShell telemetry gap troubleshooting
content: If command-line or script-block fields are absent, check whether the collector captured process-start events, whether the selected time window includes the parent event, and whether field extraction differs by host. Treat missing script content as a telemetry limitation and request the missing source or event identifiers; do not reconstruct the command.

title: Elastic PowerShell pivot query example
content: Use a staged pivot: start from the observed host, user, and time window; filter for process events whose action is process start; project only fields returned by the mapping; then correlate child process and destination activity. Replace placeholders with observed values and verify the index and field names before execution.

title: Splunk PowerShell investigation pivot
content: In Splunk, pivot from the alert's observed host or user and narrow the time range before searching for process creation and network events. Confirm the sourcetype and field extraction in returned events; a missing result means the pivot is unconfirmed, not that execution did not happen.

title: Authentication brute-force decision pattern
content: Compare failures and successes by source, account, host, and interval, then check whether the same source touched multiple accounts or produced later successful activity. Separate threshold mechanics from analyst judgment: one failed login is insufficient to label brute force.

title: Cross-provider investigation normalization
content: When correlating Elastic and Splunk results, normalize the investigation dimensions rather than field names: time window, principal, host, process, destination, outcome, and event identifier. Keep provider-specific queries in their selected skill and report which dimensions could not be compared.

title: Zero-row query interpretation
content: A zero-row result can indicate an incorrect time window, index or data view, field mismatch, delayed ingestion, or genuinely absent activity. Validate the query against a known event and record the query plus window before treating the result as an evidence gap.

title: Read-only suspicious execution playbook
content: Sequence the investigation as alert identity, event semantics, process lineage, user and host context, network pivots, historical baseline, and evidence gaps. Stop at the first unsupported pivot, preserve observed values, and leave containment or remediation as a separately authorized recommendation.
